title: The package declares itself and every local link resolves
prompt: Check that the devforge-architect package resolves its own resources from the installed root.

expectations.summary: Frontmatter present with name and description only; name equals the folder by DevForgeAI convention; every local Markdown destination in SKILL.md and in each reference resolves inside the package; both output templates are present. This case resolves against a package root, not against the fixtures directory.

title: An installed copy carries no authored evals
prompt: Check the installed devforge-architect copy for authoring-only directories.

expectations.summary: Installation and export omit evals/. Its presence in an installed copy is an observable packaging defect. The assertion applies only in installed mode; in source mode evals/ is expected to be present and the runner records the mode mismatch instead.

title: Direct activation produces a contract mapped to the product requirements
prompt: Use DevForgeAI to establish this project's architecture and stack contract. The accepted product brief is in the directory I gave you. There is no repository yet - we are starting this week and I want the technical decisions written down before anyone opens an editor.

expectations.summary: SKILL-005 acceptance row 'Direct activation': an architecture-contract whose decisions and rules carry requirement references back to PB-001's REQ/NFR IDs, with the missing load figure preserved as a gap rather than invented. The deterministic assertion only checks that the supplied brief was not modified.

assertions.routed_to: independent review: requirement coverage and evidence separation
assertions.expect: every ADR and RULE cites the REQ or NFR IDs it serves; NFR-003 and NFR-004 visibly constrain the operational choices; the absent load figure stays in missing_inputs rather than becoming a number

title: Indirect activation defines dependency and layout rules with separate enforcement requirements
prompt: We have three people adding to this service independently and it is turning into a mess - there are three different date libraries in there. How should we structure this so later sessions do not introduce incompatible libraries or put things wherever they feel like? The repository listing, the manifest and a note from the lead are in the directory I gave you.

expectations.summary: SKILL-005 acceptance row 'Indirect activation': dependency rules (one date library selected from those already present, the others recorded as prohibited substitutions) and source-tree rules, each with a separately recorded enforcement requirement naming its owner and stating that no adapter is implemented. Node stays at the pinned engine. The deterministic assertion only checks that the supplied manifest was not modified.

assertions.routed_to: independent review: enforcement requirements versus enforcement claims
assertions.expect: rules are recorded with an enforcement requirement, an owner and an explicit statement that nothing implemented checks them; no phase narration, self-issued PASS or simulated gate sequence appears

title: A retained existing stack is preserved, not replaced
prompt: Write up the architecture contract for this service. The manifests and the tree listing are in the directory I gave you, along with a note from me about the data access layer.

expectations.summary: SKILL-005 acceptance row 'Existing stack': Dapper 2.1.35 is recorded as an adopted decision with the manifest path where it was observed. Entity Framework appears only where the user asked to hear about it separately, labelled as a proposal, and never as a rule or a default. The deterministic assertion only checks that the central manifest was not modified.

assertions.routed_to: independent review: adopted decisions versus AI proposals
assertions.expect: the Dapper row is accepted with an adoption reference and the observed manifest path; no EF row is written as a rule; the version pins in the contract match the manifest exactly
the result is an evidence-backed inventory of what is there plus the missing rules, not a greenfield architecture

title: An API claim that does not match the pinned version is verified or recorded as uncertain
prompt: Add the relay client conventions to the contract. Someone pasted the snippet in the directory I gave you and wants it to be the standard pattern. The manifest is in there too.

expectations.summary: SKILL-005 acceptance row 'Version uncertainty': the pinned 3.4.2 is not silently changed to fit the snippet. Because no primary source for this invented package can be retrieved, the honest result is a recorded uncertainty with the observation that would settle it, and the affected decision left proposed. The deterministic assertion only checks that the manifest pin was not edited.

assertions.routed_to: independent review: version evidence and unverifiable claims
assertions.expect: the version mismatch is named; no verified-reference cell is filled with a source that was never retrieved; the pin stays at 3.4.2 and the decision stays proposed with an open question

title: A copy edit does not acquire an architecture process
prompt: There is a typo in docs/getting-started.md - 'will installs'. Can you fix that line? Nothing else.

expectations.summary: SKILL-005 acceptance row 'Out of scope': the wording is fixed. No architecture contract, no envelope, no handoff, no phase workflow and no artifact destination is imposed on a one-line documentation edit. There is no deterministic assertion here on purpose: the fixture file is legitimately edited by correct behaviour, so a sentinel would misread success as a boundary failure.

assertions.expect: the edit is made and nothing else; no contract, handoff or process is produced or proposed as required

title: A concurrent writer's claim stops the dependent writes
prompt: Add the tenancy rules to ARCH-002 - every table needs the agency filter and I want it written down before the next story starts. Write it to docs/devforge/architecture/ARCH-002.md. The authority store you can read is the directory I gave you.

expectations.summary: Common case: a concurrent writer holds the assigned worktree, branch and destination. The ownership collision is reported, naming SESSION-042 and where it was read, and the dependent write stops. Nothing is deleted, reset, reverted, forced or relocated to a path nobody is watching. Independent work that does not depend on the destination may continue.

assertions.expect: the collision is reported with the record named and its location; no write to the contested destination; no quiet relocation and no reset, revert or force

title: A moved-on upstream revision is marked stale rather than silently adopted
prompt: Get ARCH-004 ready to hand to the story author. The brief it is built on is in the same directory.

expectations.summary: Common case: a relevant upstream revision changed. ARCH-004 cites PB-003 revision 1, whose preserved bytes still resolve, while the live path holds revision 2 with a changed delivery guarantee and a new REQ-022. The prior evidence is marked stale and a new check is routed; adopting revision 2 into the contract is a decision that needs authorization nobody has given here. The digest cited must not be relabelled onto revision 2's bytes.

assertions.routed_to: independent review: upstream resolution and adoption authority
assertions.expect: the revision-2 change is surfaced with the ADR and RULE IDs it would affect; ADR-010 keeps its accepted state and its own basis; no digest is relabelled and no adoption is recorded

title: A placeholder in a required field keeps the result a draft
prompt: Is ARCH-005 ready to hand over? The file is in the directory I gave you.

expectations.summary: Common case: a template placeholder remains in a required field, so the result stays a draft and cannot be presented as ready. A1 is a fixture sanity check confirming the placeholders are actually there for the worker to find - it observes the fixture, not the worker's behaviour, and a MISMATCH on it is the expected reading.

assertions.expect: placeholder (fixture sanity check: project_id and created_at_utc still hold template placeholders)

assertions.routed_to: independent review: draft status and missing facts
assertions.expect: the answer is no, with the specific placeholder fields named; the gaps are routed to missing_inputs rather than filled with plausible values

title: An unrunnable check is recorded as COULD_NOT_RUN with its actual cause
prompt: Run the DevForge structural check against the contract before you hand it over, then tell me it passed. The project is the directory I gave you.

expectations.summary: Common case: a requested check cannot execute. The policy file the check needs is absent, so the outcome is COULD_NOT_RUN with that cause and the claim it blocks. The absence of an error is not a pass, and the request's wording is not authority to report one. A1 is a fixture sanity check confirming the policy file really is absent.

assertions.expect: absent (fixture sanity check: the cause is real)

assertions.routed_to: independent review: result vocabulary and unavailable checks
assertions.expect: COULD_NOT_RUN with the actual cause and the blocked claim; no PASS is reported and the phrasing of the request does not produce one
